topic: Myth vs fact / peptides your body makes: why you don't pee all night. Not just less drinking: vasopressin (ADH), released from the brain, rises at night (steady 8 AM-10 PM, significant rise 10 PM-8 AM in 11 healthy subjects; Rittig et al., Am J Physiol 1989); it inserts aquaporin-2 water channels in kidney collecting ducts so water is reabsorbed and urine is concentrated (MedlinePlus Genetics AQP2; StatPearls V2 receptor); 15 enuresis patients had a less pronounced night rise and higher night urine volume (Rittig 1989)

Fact check

Why don't you pee all night?

The claim

“You just stop drinking.”

HALF TRUE

The bigger reason is a hormone from your brain.

Meet the hormone

Vasopressin

Also called ADH. A small peptide.

Its job: save water.

The night shift

It rises while you sleep.

Day
Steady
Night
Big rise

Healthy volunteers, Rittig 1989

In the kidneys

It opens water gates.

Channels called aquaporin-2 pull water back into blood.

Night urine: less, more concentrated.

The proof

TRUE

Kids and teens who wet the bed had a smaller night rise.

They made more urine at night.

Save this for biology class.

Sources in the caption.
